items.title: NEW — style smalls from kolt's styles.vl: `flex_grow` missing beside `flex_shrink`, no `Color::current()` for `currentColor` — and the `[hidden]` HACK, which is not a small: the preflight rule loses to ANY app `display` because it sits a CASCADE LAYER below, so `View::show()` silently does nothing on every flex container
items.discussion: kolt/src/styles.vl:11-37 (three FIXMEs, one of which — `Length::full` — is already covered by `Length::pct(100f)`) and views.vl:132-139's HACK; item 4 wants a ruling, the first two want five lines each
items.status: OPEN — the owner's kolt TODO/FIXME sweep (2026-09-07)
items.body:
Three FIXMEs in kolt/src/styles.vl and one HACK in views.vl. The first two are missing siblings, the
third is not a gap at all, and the fourth is a defect wearing a HACK comment.

1. `flex_grow` — styles.vl:11-15
       // FIXME: Implement with std.
       fun flex_grow(self, value: f64) { self.raw("flex-grow", i"{value}") }
   std has `flex_shrink(self, value: f64)` (vilan/std/src/style.vl:869) and the `flex` shorthand (:865), and
   the shorthand-expansion table already names the property (`"flex" => ";flex-grow;flex-shrink;flex-basis;"`,
   style.vl:644). `flex_grow` is simply absent. Nine call sites in kolt (views.vl:104, :112, :151, :343 and
   the rest).

2. `Color::current()` — styles.vl:32-37
       // FIXME: Implement with std.
       fun current() { style::Color { text = "currentColor", root = "" } }
   std's Color constructors (style.vl:165-215) are `white`, `black`, `transparent`, `hex`, `var`, `gray`,
   `blue` — no `currentColor`. Note kolt composes it: `style::Color::current().alpha(0.1)` (channel.vl:153),
   so whatever `alpha` emits has to remain valid over a keyword color, which is worth checking as part of the
   build rather than after it.

3. `Length::full()` — styles.vl:26-30 — NOT A GAP, and the hand-written form can be deleted today.
   kolt writes `style::Length::raw("100%")`; `style::Length::pct(100f)` (style.vl:74-76) renders exactly
   `100%`. Eleven call sites (views.vl:116, :157, :252, :302, :337, :496, :513, :694, :711;
   channel.vl:136, :145) can move to `pct(100f)` with no std change. Whether std wants a `full()` alias for
   the most common percentage is taste, not a hole — decide it, but do not let it hide the two above.

4. THE `[hidden]` HACK — views.vl:132-139
       // HACK: Setting display overrides the preflight's `[hidden]` rule so the hack below toggles display.
       .child_relation("not([hidden])", "display", style::style().flex_col());
   std's preflight carries `preflight_rule("[hidden]", declarations().raw("display", "none"))`
   (style.vl:1747) with the comment "`[hidden]` last in reading order and strongest in the cascade — (0,1,0)
   against the element selectors above, so hiding still wins". Specificity is not what decides the outcome
   here: the preflight is `@layer vilan.preflight`, described in the same file as "std's floor", with the
   app's `declare` landing "one layer ABOVE this one" (style.vl:1750-1756). A cascade layer beats specificity
   outright, so ANY app style that sets `display` defeats `[hidden]`, whatever its specificity.
   The consequence reaches std's own surface, not just kolt's: `View::show(condition)`
   (vilan/std/src/browser/ui.vl:632-639) hides by `element.set_hidden(!visible)`, i.e. by the `hidden`
   property and therefore by that same preflight rule — so `show` is a no-op on every element whose style
   sets a display, which is every flex container in a real app. kolt's `child_relation("not([hidden])", ...)`
   is the workaround: put the `display` behind `:not([hidden])` so the app layer stops fighting the reset.
   OPTIONS TO RULE BETWEEN: emit the preflight `[hidden]` with `!important`; have `styled` emit a companion
   `[hidden]` rule in the APP layer alongside any `display` it writes; or make `show` toggle `display`
   directly and document that it does. Whichever wins, the pin is `show(cond)` on a flex row actually
   disappearing.

items.title: NEW — `str::parse_bool` is missing beside `parse_i32`/`parse_f64` (four call sites in kolt's preference decoders) — while the OTHER two conversions kolt hand-wrote, `bool.to_string` and `f64.to_string`, already ship as `Display` impls and can be deleted: the gap is the parse direction plus a discoverability trap on a trait method
items.discussion: kolt/src/prefs.vl:69-93, three FIXMEs; two are already covered (display.vl:54-64), the third is real
items.status: OPEN — the owner's kolt TODO/FIXME sweep (2026-09-07)
items.body:
kolt/src/prefs.vl:69-93 hand-writes three conversions, each marked `// FIXME: Implement with std.`:

    impl str {
        fun parse_bool(self): Option<bool> {
            match self { "true" => Some(true), "false" => Some(false), _ => None }
        }
    }
    impl bool { fun to_string(self): str { if self { "true" } else { "false" } } }
    impl f64  { fun to_string(self): str { i"{self}" } }

ALREADY COVERED — two of the three, deletable from kolt today. vilan/std/src/display.vl:5-7 declares
`trait Display { fun to_string(self): str }`, with `impl f64 with Display` (:54-58) and
`impl bool with Display` (:60-64), both bodied `i"{self}"` — the f64 one is byte-identical to kolt's, and
`i"{true}"` renders "true". The only real cost is DISCOVERABILITY: `to_string` is a TRAIT method, so a
module that has not imported `std::display::Display` gets "no method to_string" and reasonably concludes std
lacks it — which is precisely the visibility trap display.vl:16-21 already documents for `List::join`, with
an analyzer steer built for that one shape. The same steer should fire for `to_string`; if it does not, that
is the small build hiding in this item.

THE REAL GAP is the parse direction. `parse_i32` and `parse_f64` are `external` methods on `str` that live
in `std::option` (option.vl:292-305, sited there because their return type puts them on the `Option` chain,
per the note at :292-298). There is no `parse_bool`. kolt needs it in four of its six preference decoders
(prefs.vl:28, :40, :46, :52), each of the form `x.parse_bool().unwrap_or(false)`.

PROPOSED: `str::parse_bool(self): Option<bool>` beside `parse_i32`/`parse_f64` in option.vl, accepting
"true"/"false" only — the exact round trip of `Display::to_string`, and what `std::json`'s bool `FromJson`
(json.vl:248-260) accepts. State the three-way idiom in the doc so the next app does not hand-write any of
it: `Display::to_string` going out, `str::parse_*` coming back, `std::json`'s `Json`/`FromJson` for anything
structured.

items.title: NEW — a style-paper ruling A36 did not cover: should conditional component state COMPUTE a class list per state (`.when` today), or ride CSS variables, or data attributes via the `within`/`child_relation` machinery std already has — the owner's own first use of `when` hit the compound condition and asked, and views.vl runs `when` chains inside a signal `.map` where nobody has priced the per-notify rebuild
items.discussion: kolt/src/styles.vl:62-68; A36 (`Style::when`) CLOSED 2026-09-04, Order 27, lane std-27, vilan bb80ec4f — shipped exactly the ruling's five lines, and this is the question after it
items.status: OPEN — the owner's kolt TODO/FIXME sweep (2026-09-07)
items.body:
kolt/src/styles.vl:62-68, on the combinator A36 shipped:

    fun button_style(selected: bool, disabled: bool) {
        button_style_base
            // TODO: Investigate whether these should be computed or css vars or data attributes
            //       (performance? tidiness?).
            .when(selected, button_style_selected)
            .when(!disabled, button_style_interactive)
            .when(!selected && !disabled, button_style_interactive_events)
    }

A36 is CLOSED (tracker archive.md, 2026-09-04, Order 27, lane std-27, vilan bb80ec4f): `Style::when(condition,
delta)` landed as "exactly the ruling's five lines" — vilan/std/src/style.vl:1455-1461,
`if condition { self + delta } else { self }` — with doc guidance that own-flag chains are the intended use,
that "a compound condition is the tell for `match`", and that a later delta wins. The owner's FIRST real use
immediately produced a compound condition (`!selected && !disabled`) and a question the ruling did not reach:
whether a stateful component's style should be COMPUTED per state at all.

THE THREE CANDIDATES, AND WHAT EACH COSTS:

- COMPUTED (today's `when`): each distinct (selected, disabled) pair yields its own class-list string. The
  delta styles are emitted to the sheet once, which is the cheap part; the cost is that the app re-derives
  the string on every reactive read. That is not theoretical in kolt — views.vl:513 and :711 run `.when`
  chains INSIDE a `.map` on a signal, so the rebuild is per-notify, and `class_list` (style.vl:1465) walks
  every slot to join it.
- CSS VARIABLES: one stable class, the varying declarations written as `var(--x)` set per element. Sheet size
  flat, class attribute never changes, cost is one custom-property write per change — but a variable cannot
  vary a SELECTOR-shaped thing, and two of kolt's three deltas are exactly that (`hover`, `active` in
  `button_style_interactive_events`).
- DATA ATTRIBUTES: one class whose rules are conditioned on `[data-selected="true"]`. std ALREADY has this
  machinery — `within(name, value, inner)` (style.vl:1244) and `child_relation` (:1296), both of which check
  the attribute name and value and refuse a media-conditioned inner — and kolt already uses `within` in its
  own `select_off` (styles.vl:18-22) and `child_relation` in views.vl:138. The element's class never changes
  and toggling is one `set_attribute`. The cost is sheet size (both branches always emitted) and giving up
  the "a style is a value you can merge and pass around" property that makes `when` composable at all.

WHAT IS WANTED IS A RULING, NOT A BUILD: which of the three is the IDIOM for boolean component state; whether
`when` stays the answer for it; and whether the compound-condition steer should point at `within` rather than
at `match`. MEASURE FIRST — the per-notify class-list rebuild at views.vl:513 is the exhibit and it has never
been priced. Belongs in the style paper beside A36's record.

items.title: NEW — a `Signal<View>` (or `SignalCell<View>`) in CHILD position stringifies instead of rendering and re-rendering (kolt views.vl:543's HACK: `.swap(signal, \|x\| view)` stands in for `{signal}`); with A46's fragment the question is the same — WHAT MAY BE A CHILD (str, View, List<View>, a Signal of each), and a `View` struct cannot say it while a trait could
items.discussion: the owner's kolt find (2026-09-07), tied by the owner to A46: both may push `View` from a struct to a TRAIT; decide the child contract once, then the fragment and the signal child follow
items.status: OPEN — the owner's kolt find (2026-09-07); DESIGN with A46
items.body: Today a child `{expr}` desugars to `.child(expr)` and a `Signal<str>` child binds text; a `Signal<View>` child reaches the string path and renders the View's runtime shape. Pin it red; then rule the child contract: a `trait Child` (or `Render`) implemented by `str`, `View`, `List<View>` (A46's fragment), `Signal<str>`, `Signal<View>` and `Signal<List<View>>` — the signal impls own their re-render (a `swap` under the row's owner) — and `.child` takes `impl Child`. Whether `View` itself becomes a trait is the larger question A46 carries; the child trait does not require it and can land first.
